entry.name: fftout~
entry.digest: Output for a patcher loaded by pfft~
entry.description: The fftout~ object provides an signal output to a pfft~ object.

arguments.name: outlet-assignment
arguments.description: Determines the outlet number in thewhich will receive the output of theobject. Outlet assignments start at 1 for the leftmost outlet of. Multipleobjects will typically have different outlet numbers.

arguments.name: phase-offset
arguments.description: A second float argument tobetween 0. and 1. specifies a phase offset for the window applied to the inverse FFT performed by. A value of 0.5 for the phase offset (equivalent to 180 degrees) could potentially be helpful if using anobject directly inside thesubpatcher, since the output phase ofis shifted by 180 degrees.

arguments.name: window-envelope-function
arguments.description: Tellswhich window envelope function to use when overlapping fft's on the input signal. The options are(i.e. no window envelope),(the default), and. If the argumentis used, then thewill echo its input signal to its output without performing a Fast Fourier transform. This allows you to output raw control signals from theto the parent patcher. Note that when theoption is used, overlap-adding is still being performed to create the output signal.

attributes.name: nofft
attributes.digest: No FFT
attributes.description: With nofft set, fftout~ allows for audio to pass out from the subpatcher through pfft~s outlets without performing an inverse fft. There are a few idiosyncratic behaviors for pfft~ in the default half spectrum frame mode and pfft~ in fullspectrum mode, which for legacy reasons behave as they do.When pfft~ is in the default half spectrum mode, fftout~ ignores the windowing function, writing to the first half of the outgoing frame for the outer MSP patch.If overlap is 2, this half frame box window works out perfectly so that there is no overlap between frames. If the overlap factor is greater than 2 there are a few ways to accomodate for the overlap so that overlapping frames do not accumulate to a value N times greater than desired output.The first way is to enable @overlapscale 1. This will divide the output by the number of overlapping frames so that the sum of all overlapping frames will be averaged.The second way is to use @windowsqueeze N to squeeze the window to fit in that number of fft-hops (fftsize/overlap). For default half spectrum that should typically be set to 1 hop because of the exclusive half frame box window. For full spectrum with its default hanning window, that should typically be set to 2. This can be useful to avoid having too many overlapping frames accumulated together and then averaged.
